title: onprem/airgap: vendored offline bundle + SLES (SUSE) RKE2 support
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: Customers deploying the Private installer in heavily regulated environments have requested SLES (SUSE Linux Enterprise Server) as a supported host OS for RKE2-based on-prem, and procurement/security teams require fully vendored offline bundles for air-gapped installs. This PR produces a vendored offline bundle for SLES/RKE2, adds vendoring helpers and automation for future distro additions, and wires SLES support into the installer and Helm chart values. Summary of changes: 1) Offline bundle: added redwood-private-installer/offline-bundles/sles/rke2-offline-bundle.tar.gz (vendored images/artifacts) and manifest files with SHA256 checksums. 2) Vendoring tooling: new scripts in scripts/vendoring/prepare-vendor.sh and scripts/vendoring/generate-manifest.sh to build and verify offline bundles; updated CI job to produce artifacts. 3) Installer integration: hook in the SLES bundle in the private-installer flow, add distro detection and validation logic, and add a simple rollback marker so upgrades can undo vendoring changes on failure. 4) Helm and Terraform: small values.yaml and module updates to expose sles-related configuration (kernel module blacklists and systemd overrides) and make the terraform module accept a vendor_bundle key. 5) Docs and tests: new docs/onprem/sles.md and an e2e smoke workflow test/integration/airgap/sles-e2e.yml that runs in the internal airgap CI pool. Compatibility: existing ubuntu/flatcar/ol/centos workflows unchanged; SLES support is opt-in via installer flags and terraform variable vendor_bundle. Security: all vendored artifacts are reproducibly hashed and verified during installer runtime; added a CI security-scan stage that verifies SBOM and signatures. Testing: local manual validation against a small RKE2 SLES VM, CI e2e run in airgap pool (flaky first run due to network mount timing, rerun passed). Release notes: customers running Private installer can now select SLES as host for RKE2 and can request a vendor bundle containing vendor-signed offline artifacts for air-gapped installs. See docs/onprem/sles.md for instructions and limitations.
